title: Ramadan: the whole book again
tomorrow: the last ten: why stay up for a night nobody can name?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Sha'ban: the run-up, the month of getting ready. The alarm is set for before dawn, the dates are on the counter. Now the month itself arrives, and a sheet goes up on a wall.

A sign-up sheet is taped by the masjid door. One column of names, one column of parts of the Qur'an. Somebody's aunt has claimed the long ones. A teenager has written his name in pencil, just in case. By the month's end, between them, the whole book will have been read. That's a khatm, a completion. But why this month? The answer is a scene in Medina, in a report kept in Sahih al-Bukhari. Every night of Ramadan, the angel Jibril comes to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and the two of them go over the Qur'an together. Every year. Until one year, it changes.
screen: `A SHEET BY THE MASJID DOOR.` → `A KHATM: THE WHOLE BOOK.` → `JIBRIL, EVERY NIGHT.`

segments.voice: Start with how the Qur'an names the month. In Pickthall's words: "The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for mankind." The fast and the book belong together. The month is the book's season. Ibn 'Abbas, who tells the nightly scene, adds a detail: the Prophet was generous all year, and most generous in Ramadan, when Jibril met him, quicker to give than a blowing wind. Reading the book and opening the hand, in the same nights. Now the change. Another report says Jibril went over the Qur'an with him once each year, and in the year he died, twice. His daughter Fatima remembered him telling her quietly: twice this year. I think my time is near. So the sheet by the masjid door carries an old scene inside it. Not a race to the last page. A going-over, together, in the month the book came, the way the Prophet and Jibril did it, year after year. One to tell a friend tonight: the last Ramadan of his life was the one where the book was read through twice.
screen: `THE MONTH THE BOOK CAME DOWN.` · `JIBRIL, AND AN OPEN HAND.` · `TWICE, IN THE LAST YEAR.` · `NOT A RACE: A GOING-OVER.` · then, large: `THE BOOK IN THE MONTH.`

segments.voice: Open the Qur'an, in Arabic or in a translation, to any page, or find a recitation to listen to. Read one passage aloud, slowly, as if someone were going over it beside you. If you're keeping a khatm this year, let this be the next page of your juz'.
screen: `ONE PASSAGE, ALOUD.` · `SLOWLY, AS IF WITH SOMEONE.`

segments.voice: Ramadan: the month of fasting, which the Qur'an names as the month it was revealed. Its oldest habit is going through the book again.
Pocket this one: the book in the month, read again because it came then. Block D keeps turning.

howItsDone: In Ramadan many Muslims aim to read the whole Qur'an, alone or shared out among family or a masjid, and in some masjids the night prayers recite it through over the month.

fork.reveal: Jibril and the Prophet went over it together, night by night, through the month. the habit is a going-over, not a sprint to the last page.

chat.meaning: The Qur'an names Ramadan as the month it was revealed, and Jibril reviewed it with the Prophet each Ramadan. Going through it again is the month's habit.

khatm.meaning: a completion: reading the whole Qur'an through

Jibril.meaning: the angel Gabriel, who brought the revelation

Medina.meaning: the city where the Prophet lived his last years

juz'.meaning: one of the equal parts the Qur'an is divided into

Sahih al-Bukhari.meaning: a major collection of reports of the Prophet's words and deeds

sources.quoted: The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for mankind

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 6 (Ibn 'Abbas: Jibril met him every night of Ramadan to study the Qur'an; most generous in Ramadan, more than the blowing wind)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4998 (Jibril reviewed the Qur'an with him once a year, twice in the year he died)
Sahih al-Bukhari 3623–3624 (Fatima: he told her Jibril reviewed it twice that year, and he took it as a sign his death was near)
